evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read sink. The loop guard `while (points < lastPoint)` only ensures at least one point (2 qreals) remains, but this arm consumes six qreals and advances `types += 3` with no check that three points/types are left. With a path of elementCount=2 and types=[MoveToElement, CurveToElement], the second iteration reads 4 qreals (32 bytes) past the end of the 4-qreal points buffer: heap out-of-bounds read whose values become stroke geometry.

Origin of the only bound on the tainted points pointer: `lastPoint = points + (pointCount<<1)` (line 88) combined with this loop condition guarantees merely >= 1 point remains at each iteration, while the CurveToElement arm at lines 124-126 requires 3 points; no statement in the function supplies the missing `points + 6 <= lastPoint` check or any types-array bound.

Mirror of the out-of-bounds read in the cosmetic-pen branch: the same under-guaranteeing `while (points < lastPoint)` loop (line 167) admits iteration with one point remaining while this arm reads three QPointF values (six qreals) from the caller-supplied buffer.

Non-advancing default arm: `break` exits only the switch, leaving points and types unchanged, so the loop condition `points < lastPoint` re-enters the switch with identical state forever. A command-position type value outside MoveTo/LineTo/CurveTo (e.g. a standalone CurveToDataElement, enum value 3) in the caller-supplied types array causes an infinite loop: attacker-triggered CPU denial of service from a one-element path. The mirrored arm at lines 193-194 has the same defect.

assumptions: `path.isEmpty()` (line 9) is an internal inline not shown in this code; it is assumed to reject a zero-element path, which is the only protection for the unguarded `moveTo(points[0], points[1])` at line 139 when types == null. If a zero-count QVectorPath could report non-empty, line 139 would be an additional out-of-bounds read.

`d->strokeHandler->pts/types` are assumed to be self-growing buffer containers (internal class not shown); the allocation at line 13 is sized from `path.elementCount()+4`, consistent with subsequent appends.

The stroker/dasher callees (moveTo/lineTo/cubicTo/begin/end) are assumed to consume coordinates without memory-safety preconditions of their own; only their documented role as geometry consumers is relied on.
limitations: Signed overflow in `points + (pointCount<<1)` (line 88) requires elementCount >= 2^30, meaning the caller must already have allocated a path with over a billion elements; not practically instantiable, recorded as an integer-safety hardening note (CWE-190).
The matrix save/restore around fill() (lines 222-233) is not exception-safe, but no attacker-reachable throw is shown in this code; robustness note only.

In the common QPainter pipeline QVectorPath is produced from a well-formed QPainterPath, so the malformed-types triggers most directly affect applications that pass hand-constructed QVectorPath objects to the engine (the QVectorPath constructor performs no structural validation); this is deployment context, not a dismissal.

verdict.summary: In gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size, the attacker-controlled u32 size parameter (the declared extent of the AV1 config payload) is used at 'size -= 4;' without any check that size >= 4; the only guard, 'if (!size)', rejects zero alone. With size = 1, 2, or 3 (values inside the full domain of the box-size parameter at this parser intake point, also producible by the truncating cast '(u32) gf_bs_available(bs)'), the unsigned subtraction wraps to ~4 GiB, destroying the remaining-byte budget of the 'while (size)' OBU loop. The loop then parses, heap-allocates (gf_malloc), copies, and retains (gf_list_add) OBU data across the entire remaining bitstream, far beyond the declared config extent, until a parse error or allocation failure - attacker-driven unbounded resource consumption (memory retention with large per-entry overhead and CPU) and loss of the box boundary, i.e., a denial of service on the process parsing the malicious file.

evidence.reason: Unsigned underflow sink: the remaining-bytes budget 'size' is decremented by the 4-byte header size with no prior check that size >= 4. For attacker-supplied size in {1,2,3} (full u32 domain of the box-size parameter), the subtraction wraps to ~0xFFFFFFFD, so the subsequent 'while (size)' loop treats ~4 GiB as remaining and parses, gf_malloc-copies, and gf_list_add-retains OBU data beyond the declared config extent until parse failure or allocation failure - unbounded attacker-driven resource consumption (DoS). The mention sweep found no other statement constraining size: 'if (!size)' (lines 8-9) rejects only 0, and 'if (size<obu_size)' (line 72) executes after the wrap.

Origin of the tainted value: 'size' is a u32 parameter of this exported config-parser entry point; its producer (the box-size field of the attacker-supplied container) is not shown in this code, so per the width-domain rule its surface is the full u32 domain, including the sub-4 values 1-3 that trigger the underflow at 'size -= 4;'. No documented or asserted precondition on size exists anywhere in the function.

evidence.snippet:
if (!size) size = (u32) gf_bs_available(bs);
	if (!size) return NULL;
evidence.reason: Contributing statements: the truncating cast '(u32) gf_bs_available(bs)' can itself produce a sub-4 size (e.g. an available count of 0x100000002 truncates to 2) even when 4+ bytes exist, and the only guard present, 'if (!size) return NULL;', rejects zero alone - edge-tested at size = 1, 2, 3 it passes, leaving the underflow at 'size -= 4;' unguarded on every path.

assumptions: gf_av1_parse_obu, gf_bs_read_int, gf_bs_read_data, gf_bs_available, gf_bs_seek, gf_malloc, GF_SAFEALLOC, gf_list_add are GPAC-internal/standard helpers whose semantics are taken per discipline 3: bitstream reads clamp at end-of-stream, allocation returns pointer-or-NULL, gf_list_add appends.

obu_size is filled by the unshown callee gf_av1_parse_obu and is therefore attacker-data over the full u64 domain; the code's own 'if (size<obu_size)' (u64 promotion, no truncation) is the only local bound on it and executes after the alloc/read pair.

The bitstream 'bs' is presumed to span data beyond the declared config extent (the function takes an explicit size parameter precisely to bound consumption within it); the extent bound is what the underflow destroys.
limitations: Potential infinite loop / unbounded list growth if gf_av1_parse_obu ever returns GF_OK with obu_size == 0: the loop seeks back to pos, re-parses the identical bytes, and each iteration leaks a GF_AV1_OBUArrayEntry into cfg->obu_array. Not made primary because it depends on unshown callee behavior (parse returning a zero size with GF_OK) plus gf_malloc(0) returning non-NULL; the 'assert(obu_size == gf_bs_get_position(bs) - pos)' would abort in debug builds and is a no-op under NDEBUG.

Unchecked short read: gf_bs_read_data's return (bytes actually read) is ignored and 'a->obu_length = obu_size' is set unconditionally (lines 67-68), so an obu_size larger than the remaining stream leaves uninitialized heap retained in the returned config (CWE-908). The disclosure impact requires consumers of cfg->obu_array that are not shown in this code, so the chain is not instantiated here.
'assert(obu_size == gf_bs_get_position(bs) - pos)' is a debug-only consistency check (no-op under NDEBUG) and cannot be relied on as a guard in release builds.

If the underlying gf_bs_read_data/parse layer happened to fail immediately at the declared box end, the over-parsing impact would shrink, but that protection would live in an unshown callee and cannot be treated as a guard.

verdict.summary: QPaintEngineEx::stroke iterates the caller-supplied QVectorPath with only 'while (points < lastPoint)' as a bound, which guarantees merely 2 remaining coordinates, yet the CurveToElement arm passes points[0]..points[5] (6 coordinates) to cubicTo, so a path whose trailing curve element lacks 3 points causes an out-of-bounds read of up to 4 qreals (both in the non-cosmetic and cosmetic branches). Independently, the switch's 'default: break;' arms advance neither points nor types, so any element-type value not matching Move/Line/CurveTo (e.g. the defined CurveToDataElement value in attacker-supplied types data) makes the loop condition permanently true, hanging the process with unbounded CPU from a tiny input.

evidence.snippet:
case QPainterPath::CurveToElement:
                    d->activeStroker->cubicTo(points[0], points[1],
                                              points[2], points[3],
                                              points[4], points[5]);
evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The only guard on points is 'while (points < lastPoint)' (line 111), which admits an iteration with just 2 coordinates remaining, but this sink reads points[0]..points[5] (6 coordinates) before 'points += 6'. Trigger instantiated: path with elementCount=1 (2 qreals of points) and types={CurveToElement} reaches cubicTo reading 4 qreals past the buffer; the values then flow into fill() at line 157.

Second site of the same out-of-bounds read in the cosmetic-pen branch: 'while (points < lastPoint)' at line 167 guarantees only 2 coordinates, but ((const QPointF *)points)[0..2] consumes 6; a trailing CurveToElement with fewer than 3 points reads past the end of the points buffer.

Infinite loop (CWE-835). For an element-type value matching none of the three cases (e.g. the defined CurveToDataElement value in attacker-controlled types data), the default arm advances neither points nor types, so 'while (points < lastPoint)' at line 111 remains permanently true: unbounded CPU consumption (denial of service) from a two-element input. The mirrored default at lines 193-194 has the same defect.

Origin of the tainted values: the points array, types array, and count are taken verbatim from the caller-supplied path with no consistency validation; lastPoint is the only bound ever computed, and nothing verifies that the types array can supply the entries the loop consumes ('types += 3') or that each curve element has its 3 points.

assumptions: The QVectorPath contents (points, types, elementCount) are treated as attacker-data per the width-domain rule: their producers are not shown in this code, and stroke() is a public virtual paint-engine entry point that consumes paths frequently derived from parsed graphics content; no statement in this code narrows the types values or the points/types/count consistency.

QVectorPath::isEmpty() is relied on (line 9) to mean elementCount()==0, per the universally known container-semantics allowance; it guarantees the initial moveTo(points[0], points[1]) reads (lines 139, 203) stay in bounds.
limitations: Integer overflow at line 13 ('path.elementCount()+4') and line 88 ('pointCount<<1') requires a path with roughly 2^30 or more points (tens of gigabytes of coordinate data); not treated as a primary finding.
The unchecked 'new StrokeHandler(...)' at line 13 relies on throwing C++ new; failure terminates the process and is not attacker-instantiable.

The '*types' out-of-bounds read (types array shorter than the point stream, line 112/128 with 'types += 3') is a facet of the same missing points/types/count validation recorded as the primary CWE-125 finding, not a separate defect.
The division at line 42 ('extent / patternLength') is safe: the quoted guard 'if (qFuzzyIsNull(patternLength))' at line 40 routes to Qt::NoPen before the division executes.

verdict.summary: In the charwise-Visual branch, get_visual_text() computes the selection length *lenp directly from the unclamped cursor/Visual columns (lines 24/29) without ever bounding it to the actual line length, then dereferences *pp + (*lenp - 1) at the mb_ptr2len call. The only guards present (lnum equality, **pp == NUL testing just the first byte, and *lenp > 0 testing the lower bound) do not constrain the end offset, so a selection whose end column lies past the line's terminating NUL (e.g. with 'virtualedit' or a stale Visual position) causes a heap out-of-bounds read at line 35 and returns an oversized length to the caller.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read sink. *lenp is derived from raw selection columns with no upper bound; *pp + (*lenp - 1) can point past the line buffer's NUL. Simulated trigger: line "ab" (3-byte allocation), VIsual.col = 0, cursor.col = 6 -> *lenp = 7 at line 29, **pp = 'a' so the line-31 guard does not fire, line-33 guard passes (7 > 0), and line 35 reads line+6, four bytes past the allocation; mb_ptr2len then reads further OOB bytes and inflates *lenp (up to 10) which is returned to the caller.

Taint origin (mirror of line 24). The selection length is computed solely from VIsual.col and curwin->w_cursor.col, editor-state offsets whose producers are not shown in this code and which are never compared against the line length or clamped anywhere on the path to the line-35 sink, so any column value past the end of the line flows directly into the out-of-bounds pointer arithmetic.

assumptions: Unshown callees are treated per standard semantics only: ml_get_pos/ml_get_curline return pointers into the current line buffer, mb_ptr2len (utf_ptr2len) returns at least 1 and may read up to 4 bytes at the given position, unadjust_for_sel adjusts 'selection' option semantics, LT_POS compares lnum then col, reset_VIsual_and_resel resets selection state.

VIsual.col and curwin->w_cursor.col are struct fields set by code not shown here; per the width-domain rule their input surface is the full range of the column type, and no statement in this code narrows them to the line length.
has_mbyte depends on runtime encoding; the defect requires it set, which is the common multibyte configuration.
limitations: The oversized *lenp is returned to unseen callers (operators such as rot13/case change applied to the last Visual selection) that write in place; a heap out-of-bounds WRITE is plausible there, but that impact link is in code not given, so only the out-of-bounds read at line 35 is claimed as the primary defect.
A secondary scenario where the start anchor itself lies past the NUL makes **pp (line 31) an out-of-bounds read too; it shares the same root cause (unbounded columns) and is not counted separately.
Signed overflow of *lenp (colA - colB + 1 near INT_MAX) is speculative: no quoted limit admits such columns, but none is instantiable from the shown code either.

verdict.summary: The EditDistance kernel never validates the rank of the attacker-controlled sparse shapes. With a rank-1 truth/hypothesis sparse input, group_dims is empty, output_shape becomes a scalar (dims()==0) that still passes the `output_elements > 0` check, and `output_strides[output_shape.dims() - 1] = 1;` indexes an empty vector with -1 (size_t SIZE_MAX), an out-of-bounds write at data()-8 (near-nullptr, deterministic crash; formally a memory-corruption primitive).

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write sink. When the attacker supplies rank-1 truth/hypothesis shapes, group_dims has size 0, the loop at line 50 adds no dims, output_shape.dims()==0, and output_strides is an empty vector (data()==nullptr); this statement computes index 0-1 = -1, which std::vector::operator[] takes as size_t SIZE_MAX, writing int64(1) at nullptr-8. No check anywhere in this code requires output_shape.dims() > 0 or truth rank >= 2; the nearby `output_elements > 0` check passes because a scalar output has 1 element.

Origin of the tainted value: truth_st_shape's rank is derived entirely from the attacker-controlled truth_shape tensor contents. A shape tensor with a single element (e.g. [2]) yields dims()==1, and nothing in this code constrains that rank to >= 2, which drives group_dims to size 0 and the output shape to rank 0 at the sink on line 66.

assumptions: ValidateShapes (lines 15-18) and sparse::SparseTensor::Create (lines 34-42) are not shown; per the analysis rules their contents cannot serve as guards and were not relied upon. Rank-1 sparse tensors with a matching order vector [0] are ordinary in-domain inputs these standard constructors accept.
The loc bounds checks `0 <= loc && loc < output_elements` preceding each output_t(loc) write were verified correct at both bounds and are treated as effective guards for those sinks.
limitations: Secondary crash path: a rank-0 truth shape (0-element shape tensor) makes line 46 `std::vector<int64_t> group_dims(truth_st_shape.dims() - 1)` construct a vector of size SIZE_MAX, throwing std::length_error and aborting the process (DoS); reachability depends on the unshown validators accepting rank-0 sparse tensors with [N,0] index matrices, so it was not counted as a primary finding.

Rank-mismatched inputs (e.g. hypothesis rank < truth rank) may hit CHECK failures in TensorShape::dim_size (line 51) or sparse::Group, but the shown code passes sorted_order sized from the truth rank to both SparseTensor::Create calls, which likely rejects mismatches earlier; behavior depends on unshown code.

Potential dtype CHECK crash via `vec<int64_t>()` if a non-int64 shape tensor is supplied, and potential num_elements overflow with extreme dim products, both depend on unshown validation and were not instantiated.

The out-of-bounds write at line 66 targets a fixed near-null address (nullptr-8) with constant value 1, so the practical impact is a deterministic crash (denial of service) rather than a controllable corruption primitive.

verdict.summary: The function is memory-safe as written: the scalar k is constrained to [1, n-1] by a quoted range check before its modular-inverse and scalar-multiplication uses, all RNG failure sentinels are tested before the filled buffers are consumed, s is verified to fit curve->num_bytes before being written into the signature, and every copy/write length derives from curve constants rather than attacker data. The only unvalidated pass-through, hash_size into the unshown internal helper bits2int, has no instantiated harmful use in this code.

assumptions: curve points to a valid static curve descriptor of the library; num_words, num_n_words and num_bytes derived from it are internally consistent and bounded by uECC_MAX_WORDS.
regularize_k returns a carry of 0 or 1, so k2[carry] and k2[!carry] index the two-element array in bounds; the same fixed local buffers tmp and s back both slots.

uECC_generate_random_int, uECC_vli_* arithmetic, EccPoint_mult and bits2int behave per the upstream micro-ecc library; the failure sentinel of uECC_generate_random_int is nonetheless checked locally in this code (quoted in STEP 2).

signature is caller-allocated with at least 2*curve->num_bytes bytes and private_key/message_hash are caller-allocated with the declared sizes; these are standard library interface contracts not documented inside the given code.
limitations: hash_size (unsigned, full 32-bit domain) is passed to the internal helper bits2int without any local check, clamp, or mask; the mention sweep found no other statement touching it. If a caller misdeclares hash_size and the not-shown bits2int advances message_hash by (hash_size - num_bytes), an out-of-bounds read would occur inside that callee. The harmful use is not in this code and the callee's behavior is not characterizable from what is given, so the impact chain is not instantiated here.

For curves where num_n_words exceeds num_words (e.g. secp160r1), the value in the top word of s is deliberately initialized by s[num_n_words - 1] = 0 before the num_n_words-wide modular operations; this was verified as an initialization statement, not a defect.

verdict.summary: No memory-safety defect is reachable in this code. All register indices and argument counts reaching sinks are bounded by quoted guards (idx > 0, idx != sp, n < 0 sentinel handling, n < 14 clamps, and a fully-enumerated switch with rejecting default); remaining candidates require malformed ASTs or misbehaving internal callees that this code does not and cannot instantiate.

assumptions: The AST (tree, rhs) is well-formed per node type (e.g. NODE_CALL nodes carry recv/mid/args links): this structure is produced by the parser, which is not shown, and per analysis rules an unshown producer cannot supply a trigger.

Internal helpers push()/pop()/cursp() maintain the register-stack ceiling (codegen_error on over-complex expressions) and gen_values(s, ..., limit) respects its limit parameter; lv_idx returns either 0 (not-a-local sentinel, rejected by 'if (idx > 0)') or an in-frame register index.
codegen(s, node, VAL) leaves the generated value in the register below cursp() (the convention making 'int recv = cursp()-1;' valid after receiver codegen).
limitations: The 'if (n == 14)' keyword-argument consolidation branch is unreachable: the gen_values limit is 13 whenever keyword arguments exist ('(tree->cdr->car)?13:14'), so gen_values can never return 14 there; it is harmless dead defensive code.

In the NODE_SCALL path, when 'val || sp == cursp()' is false the source value register sp is not copied into the retval slot before receiver/argument codegen, so 'gen_move(s, cursp(), sp, 0)' (rhs==NULL case) can later read a stale register. This is a within-frame wrong-value miscompilation (the known upstream mruby safe-navigation assignment bug, fixed in later releases); the trigger is instantiable from this code's own statements but the impact is wrong bytecode, not an out-of-bounds access, corruption, bypass, or amplification, so it does not qualify as a vulnerability.

NULL-dereference candidates at 'tree->cdr->cdr->car' and similar node field accesses would require the parser (producer not shown) to emit structurally malformed nodes; this precondition could not be instantiated from the given code.

verdict.summary: The attacker-controlled byte-accumulation loop writing into command[MaxTextExtent] is provably in-bounds: the post-increment check ((size_t)(p-command) < (MaxTextExtent-1)) caps data writes at index MaxTextExtent-2 and the terminating NUL at MaxTextExtent-1, inside the MaxTextExtent-sized buffer; all other attacker-data sinks (sscanf into memset-initialized doubles, LocaleNCompare on always-NUL-terminated tokens, FormatLocaleString/CopyMagickString with matching MaxTextExtent bounds) are bounded by quoted statements, and no memory or allocation is sized by attacker-derived MediaBox/CropBox dimensions.

assumptions: AcquireString("") is assumed to allocate slack of at least the ~60 bytes the fixed formats "%gx%g", "2.0x2.0" and "-g%.20gx%.20g " can produce; AcquireString's allocation size is not shown, but per analysis rules an unshown callee contract can never produce a trigger, and the written content is bounded by the fixed formats regardless.

GetDelegateCommands(delegate_info) is assumed to return a non-NULL format string with placeholders matching the six arguments passed; it originates from operator-controlled delegates.xml, not from attacker data, and delegate_info NULL is checked.
ThrowReaderException and the Destroy*/Relinquish* helpers are assumed to perform their documented cleanup and return; their internals are not shown.
image_info fields (page, ping, monochrome, number_scenes, antialias) are operator/API configuration rather than file-originator data; the file blob is the trust boundary crossed here.
limitations: width=(size_t) floor(bounds.x2-bounds.x1+0.5) performs an attacker-influenced double-to-size_t conversion that is undefined behavior for negative or oversized MediaBox/CropBox values (e.g. 'MediaBox [100 100 0 0'), but in this code the resulting huge page.width/height only reach bounded FormatLocaleString calls and the image->page struct assignment; no memory operation in this code is sized by them, so no in-code impact is instantiated.

An attacker-controlled huge MediaBox flows into the '-g<width>x<height>' GhostPCL delegate option and could induce unbounded raster allocation inside the external GhostPCL process (CWE-400-style amplification); the impact lands entirely in the not-shown delegate, so it is speculative for this code.

(void) AcquireUniqueFilename(read_info->filename) ignores the failure sentinel; if it fails, the delegate output would target the original input filename. The trigger requires an environment/allocation failure the attacker cannot instantiate.

On the delegate_info == NULL early return path, the temporary input_filename created by AcquireUniqueSymbolicLink is never relinquished, leaking one temp file per failed invocation; this depends on delegate configuration, not attacker input.

In the number_scenes != 0 branch, FormatLocaleString(options,...) overwrites the previously built '-g' geometry option, dropping the page geometry from the delegate invocation; functional quirk with no security effect.
The geometry buffer is formatted but never used afterward (dead store); cosmetic only.

verdict.summary: issuerAndThisUpdateCheck() fails to verify that the quoted issuer/thisUpdate value contains a closing double quote before advancing past it. When the string is unterminated, the scan loops exit with is->bv_len == x.bv_len (or tu->bv_len == x.bv_len), and 'x.bv_len -= is->bv_len + 1' / 'x.bv_len -= tu->bv_len + 1' underflows the unsigned ber_len_t to a huge value while x.bv_val is advanced one byte past the end of the input buffer. Subsequent reads (x.bv_val[0] in the space-eating loop and the comma check, strncasecmp probes, and any further quote-scan bounded by the wrapped length) read out of bounds, with a scan bound near SIZE_MAX that can walk the heap until a fault. A client-supplied attribute value such as '{thisUpdate "AAAA...(24)...A}' (38 bytes, no closing quote) triggers the out-of-bounds read on every request, enabling remote crash of the validating process.

evidence.reason: The scan loop at line 107 ('for ( ; tu->bv_len < x.bv_len; tu->bv_len++ )') exits by its own condition when no closing '"' exists in the remainder, yielding tu->bv_len == x.bv_len. These statements then advance x.bv_val one byte past the buffer end and subtract tu->bv_len + 1 from x.bv_len, underflowing the unsigned ber_len_t to ~SIZE_MAX. No check that a terminator was found exists on any path. Trigger: input '{thisUpdate "' + 24 non-quote bytes + '}' (38 bytes) passes the line 19/21 checks and reaches this defect.

Identical twin defect in the issuer branch: the loop at line 65 can exit without finding a closing '"' (is->bv_len == x.bv_len), so this subtraction underflows x.bv_len and moves x.bv_val one past the allocation. Trigger: '{issuer rdnSequence:"' + >=16 non-quote bytes + '}' with total length >= 38.

First out-of-bounds read consuming the underflowed state: after the wrapped subtraction, x.bv_val points one past the input buffer and x.bv_len is huge, so this loop dereferences x.bv_val[0] out of bounds and, if that heap byte is a space, scans forward with no effective length bound (~SIZE_MAX) — an unbounded heap over-read (line 130 repeats the OOB read if the byte is not a space).

assumptions: ber_len_t is unsigned (standard OpenLDAP typedef 'typedef unsigned long ber_len_t'); the code's own subtraction at lines 79/113 relies on it. Even if it were signed, x.bv_len becomes negative, keeping every later condition ('&& x.bv_len', loop bounds) true, so the OOB reads still occur.
'in' carries a client-supplied attribute value being validated by this syntax checker; its bv_val/bv_len content and length are attacker-data per the width-domain rule.
slap_sl_malloc/ber_dupbv_x are allocation helpers per discipline 3 (return pointer or NULL); their returns are consumed unchecked at lines 142/148.
limitations: Lines 142/148: return values of ber_dupbv_x and slap_sl_malloc are not checked for NULL; trigger requires allocation failure an attacker cannot induce (robustness, not a vulnerability here).

Pre-underflow reads such as x.bv_val[0] in the space-eating loops before the '&& x.bv_len' test, and strncasecmp probing past x.bv_len, stay in bounds because the trailing '}' (guaranteed by line 21) always terminates them; they become the OOB sinks only via the underflow defects above.

The dquote-unescaping copy loop (lines 149-155) was verified in-bounds: dst never exceeds is->bv_len - numdquotes, the NUL lands at the last allocated byte, and the one-past-is read on a trailing quote pair lands on the still-allocated closing quote.

Whether the OOB read discloses data to the attacker is not shown (error paths return without echoing parsed bytes); the demonstrated impact is the out-of-bounds read itself and a likely process crash (denial of service).

verdict.summary: uECC_sign_with_k passes the unvalidated attacker-controllable parameter hash_size (full unsigned domain, no narrowing contract quoted) directly into bits2int(), which converts message_hash bytes into the fixed stack array tmp[uECC_MAX_WORDS]. hash_size is mentioned exactly once in the code (at the sink), so no check, clamp, mask, or truncation exists on any path; an oversized hash_size drives a stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length and content.

evidence.reason: Root cause: the attacker-derived size hash_size is passed raw into the byte-to-native conversion writing into the fixed stack buffer `uECC_word_t tmp[uECC_MAX_WORDS]` (line 8) with no bounds check anywhere on any path (mention sweep: hash_size appears only here and in its declaration). Trigger instantiated with hash_size larger than the curve's byte length (any unsigned value is in-domain since no quoted contract narrows it), producing a stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length and content.

Origin of the tainted value: hash_size enters as an unsigned parameter whose producer is not shown in this code; its input surface is the full unsigned domain (0 to 0xFFFFFFFF), and no statement of this code narrows it before it reaches the bits2int sink at line 61.

assumptions: curve fields (num_words, num_n_bits, num_bytes, n, G) are treated as library-defined compile-time constants bounded by uECC_MAX_WORDS; if curve fields were attacker-settable, additional overflows (e.g. `s[num_n_words - 1] = 0;`) would follow, but the exported curve selection API is not shown and is same-trust-domain.
The `signature` output buffer is assumed to hold 2*curve->num_bytes bytes per the documented library API contract (caller-side allocation, same trust domain as the signing operator).

Internals of bits2int, regularize_k, uECC_vli_* and EccPoint_mult are not shown; per the analysis rules their potential leniency was NOT used to dismiss the primary candidate — the defect is the absent local validation at the call site.
uECC_MAX_WORDS is assumed to be the largest supported curve's word count, so all curve-derived fixed-size operations on tmp/s/p are within their declared bounds.
limitations: The concrete overflowing copy occurs inside bits2int (not shown); the finding is anchored at the call site per the rule that passing a raw attacker size into a copy/conversion operation is a defect at the call, and dismissing it as 'the callee clamps it' would be an unquoted-contract dismissal.

When g_rng_function is NULL, blinding is disabled (tmp[0] = 1), leaving the modular inverse of k observable to timing analysis — a documented side-channel degradation, not a defect meeting the impact taxonomy of this analysis.

verdict.summary: issuerAndThisUpdateCheck fails to verify that the quoted issuer/thisUpdate value ended on a real closing quote before consuming is->bv_len + 1 / tu->bv_len + 1 bytes from the remaining window. verdict.summary: This is the upstream Linux kernel BPF ringbuf reserve path (kernel/bpf/ringbuf.c) and it validates its attacker-facing inputs correctly: the u64 size is bounded by the RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ check before any arithmetic (no overflow of size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, no truncation into the u32 len given the constant's upstream value UINT_MAX>>2), the header placement is masked by rb->mask, and the space check new_prod_pos - cons_pos > rb->mask fails safe in the unsigned-underflow direction even though userspace can write the mmap'd consumer_pos page. rb->mask is (ringbuf_size - 1) for a power-of-two size, an invariant set at map allocation time in the same subsystem (bpf_ringbuf_alloc), and the data pages are mapped twice contiguously so records straddling the logical end remain inside the allocation.

limitations: Hypothetical u64 overflow or u32 truncation at 'len = round_up(size + BPF_RINGBUF_HDR_SZ, 8)' would require RINGBUF_MAX_RECORD_SZ to be near 2^32 or 2^64; no statement in this code or width-domain rule can instantiate that, since the constant is a fixed compile-time literal, so this candidate is speculative.

A NULL rb passed by the caller would crash the kernel, but producing NULL requires the unshown map-lookup/dispatch contract to be violated and the crash occurs at the privilege of the BPF program's owner (BPF load requires CAP_BPF/CAP_SYS_ADMIN); not instantiated as a vulnerability in this code.

The consumer side that later parses hdr->len and hdr->pg_off, and bpf_ringbuf_rec_pg_off itself, are not shown; any misuse there could not be attributed to this snippet, and the values this code stores are within the domains those consumers expect under the assumptions above.

verdict.summary: This function is a thin batch-orchestration loop. The only attacker-influenced value that gates processing, dl_type, is narrowed by the quoted comparisons against htons(ETH_TYPE_IP) and htons(ETH_TYPE_IPV6) before ipf_handle_frag is called; packet pointers come from the batch iteration macro; pb_idx is capped by the loop bound pb_cnt from dp_packet_batch_size(pb); and the lock/unlock pair is correctly matched on every path. verdict.summary: ex_copy consumes the Ex-command parameters line1, line2 and n with no bounds validation anywhere in this function and passes them as raw line indices into memory-line indexing operations. The destination n is stored unvalidated into curwin->w_cursor.lnum and used as the insertion index for ml_append, giving an out-of-domain index into the buffer's line store; line1 is likewise fed unvalidated to ml_get. That index was set directly from the unvalidated parameter n (line 28) and is never compared against the buffer's line range on any path (mention sweep over all mentions of n and the cursor: lines 9, 10, 25, 28, 40, 50 — none is a bounds guard). Trigger: n = 1000000000 with a 1-line buffer passes u_save's sentinel check (nothing provably makes it FAIL) and drives an out-of-bounds insertion index; n = LONG_MAX additionally overflows n+1 at lines 9 and 25.

Taint origin: the attacker-data parameter n (handler-function argument, full linenr_T signed width, producer not shown) is stored into the cursor with no range check, establishing the out-of-domain index consumed at the line 36 sink.

Second sink of the same root cause: the unvalidated parameter line1 is used directly as a line index for the read accessor ml_get, and its return is consumed with no sentinel check. The loop condition `while (line1 <= line2)` only bounds line1 relative to the equally unvalidated line2 (line1 = line2 = 1000000000 satisfies it against a 1-line buffer), so an out-of-range value reaches this read immediately.

assumptions: linenr_T is a signed integer type (long in Vim/Neovim), so the parameter domain includes negative values and values up to the type maximum; the producing address parser is not shown in this code.
curbuf, curwin and cmdmod are globals set outside this code; the buffer's line count (the bound the sinks require) is never referenced by any statement in this function.

ml_get, ml_append, u_save, appended_lines_mark are project-internal callees whose out-of-range behavior is not shown; per the call-site rule the defect stands at the lines that pass raw indices into them.
limitations: In the complete Vim/Neovim codebase the Ex-command framework (do_one_cmd/get_address) is generally understood to validate command ranges and destination addresses against the buffer; that validation is not present in the given code and could not be quoted, so parameters were classified as attacker-data per the width-domain rule. With the full caller in view this function may be safe in context.

If u_save(n, n + 1) returns FAIL for out-of-range n (lines 25-26), the early return would block the C1 trigger before the cursor assignment; u_save's contract is not shown, so this could not be verified either way.

count = line2 - line1 + 1 (line 6) and n + 1 (lines 9, 25) can overflow at width-extreme parameter values (CWE-190); these are treated as manifestations of the same missing range validation rather than an independent primary defect.

verdict.summary: esp_output_head consumes attacker-influenced skb state and packet-derived sizes, but every sink is guarded by a quoted, operator-correct check in execution order: the tailroom comparison 'tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)' admits exactly-at-limit and blocks one-past-limit; the strict 'nr_frags < MAX_SKB_FRAGS' bound keeps the page-descriptor index in range; the refill failure sentinel is tested before pfrag's first use with a fallback to the COW path; the skb_cow_data negative-return sentinel is tested before trailer's first use; and the esp header pointer is saved as an offset before COW and restored after, surviving the reallocation skb_cow_data may perform. Residual hazards (negative tailen from an unsigned int wider than 2^31, a stale esp->esph if esp_output_encap reallocated the skb, nr_frags TOCTOU, esph_offset int truncation, fill_trailer extent) all require unshown-callee behavior or packet-derived values far outside the widths a network peer can instantiate, so they are recorded as limitations, not vulnerabilities.

assumptions: skb_cow_data(skb, tailen, &trailer) honors its documented kernel contract: on a return >= 0 it guarantees 'tailen' bytes of tailroom in '*trailer'; the code checks the negative sentinel 'if (nfrags < 0) goto out;' before first use.

skb_page_frag_refill(allocsize, pfrag, GFP_ATOMIC) returning true guarantees at least 'allocsize' (>= tailen) bytes available from pfrag->offset in pfrag->page; the sentinel is checked with an error arm that releases x->lock and falls back to the COW path before pfrag is used.

esp_output_encap(x, skb, esp) does not reallocate the skb; if it did, esp->esph would already dangle when 'esph_offset = (unsigned char *)esp->esph - skb_transport_header(skb);' is computed, and the restored 'esp->esph = (struct ip_esp_hdr *)(skb_transport_header(skb) + esph_offset);' would be a wild pointer. This callee is not shown, so its non-reallocating behavior is an unquotable contract.

esp_output_fill_trailer(tail, esp->tfclen, esp->plen, esp->proto) writes no more than tfclen + 2 bytes and the caller-computed tailen covers that extent; the callee is not shown, so this is an assumption.

The caller computes esp->tailen/plen/tfclen from skb length plus SA parameters; packet-derived lengths on the XFRM output path are bounded well below 2^31, but the caller arithmetic itself is not shown.
pskb_put performs its own kernel BUG_ON bound for the trailer==skb case; the local guard 'tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)' already ensures it cannot trigger.
limitations: Speculative: if esp->tailen (unsigned) exceeded INT_MAX, 'int tailen = esp->tailen;' would go negative and 'tailen <= skb_tailroom(skb)' would under-admit, leading to pskb_put with a negative length and esp_output_fill_trailer writing at the tail. No trust-boundary party can instantiate a >2^31 tailen because the packet source (IP total length <= 65535, GRO/GSO aggregation of at most hundreds of KB) bounds it far below that scale.

Speculative: a stale esp->esph would result if esp_output_encap reallocated the skb (e.g. via pskb_expand_head) before 'esph_offset' is computed; the precondition lives entirely inside an unshown callee. The code itself demonstrates awareness of reallocation by saving and restoring the header offset across skb_cow_data.

Speculative: int truncation of 'esph_offset' would require the ESP header and the transport header to sit more than 2GB apart inside a single skb head allocation, which no reachable skb construction in this code can produce.

Speculative: a TOCTOU on skb_shinfo(skb)->nr_frags between the else-if test and the locked re-read would need a second context mutating the same in-transmission skb; no such context, re-entry point, or lock-release window exists in this code.

The skb being processed may carry content from a remote-originated forwarded packet; its fields are attacker-influenced but every use of them in this function (tailroom, nr_frags, frag_list, cloned state) is guarded by the quoted checks above.

verdict.summary: In ReshapeSparseTensor, attacker-supplied target_shape dims (int64 tensor content, only guarded by `size >= 0` which admits values up to INT64_MAX) are multiplied into the int64 accumulator `product *= size;` with no overflow bound anywhere in the code. Trigger: target_shape = [INT64_MAX, 2] (or [2^62+1, 2^62+1, -1]) makes the accumulated product exceed INT64_MAX, executing signed-overflow UB at this line; subsequent checks are computed on the wrapped value and huge dims reach TensorShape, causing at minimum process abort (DoS).
Taint origin: attacker-controlled int64 element of the target_shape tensor read with no range validation; its full declared width reaches the unchecked multiply at line 44.

assumptions: TensorShape construction and AddDim (lines 20, 45, 82, 92) CHECK-fail on negative dims or element-count overflow; this characterizes the abort consequence of the overflow but is project-internal behavior not shown in the given code.
The ReshapeSparseTensorFunctor body is not shown; its memory safety could not be analyzed and it neither proves nor disproves the primary defect.

The harmful use would occur entirely inside the not-shown functor and this code passes individually in-domain arguments, so this is recorded rather than confirmed; it is an intake-validation gap worth fixing.

Dense_size/nnz allocation at lines 90-93 (TensorShape({nnz, output_rank})) can overflow int64 with attacker-chosen nnz and output_rank, causing a CHECK-abort (DoS) inside TensorShape; same intake gap as the primary defect but its harmful statement is inside the callee.

No out-of-bounds write was simulated: even when the overflowed product lets the divisibility checks pass, output index writes in the functor remain within the allocated {nnz, output_rank} buffer, so impact is UB/abort rather than confirmed memory corruption.

verdict.summary: ReadCINImage copies attacker-controlled raster bytes into the quantum scanline buffer using a row length computed from the file-controlled bits_per_pixel field (up to 255) without any comparison against the buffer capacity: the capacity measure 'extent=GetQuantumExtent(...)' is computed and explicitly discarded via '(void) extent;'. With depth>32 the computed length exceeds the 32-bit-quantum buffer capacity, and 'ReadBlobStream(image,length,pixels,&count)' writes past the end of the heap buffer (heap out-of-bounds write with attacker-controlled file content).

evidence.reason: Sink: 'length' is derived from the file-controlled depth (bits_per_pixel, full 0..255 domain) and is passed as the byte count for a copy into 'pixels', the quantum scanline buffer, with no bounds check on any path; with depth=255, columns=1, rows=4096 and a 1536-byte file, 96 bytes are copied into a 12-byte-capacity buffer (extent), an 84-byte heap out-of-bounds write at the first row iteration.

Missing-check site: the code computes its own buffer-capacity measure 'extent' and explicitly discards it with '(void) extent;' instead of validating 'length' against it; the only sentinel test ('if (count != (ssize_t) length)') runs after the copy and the earlier blob-size check (line 350) bounds the file at columns*rows/8 bits, not the buffer.

Taint origin: the attacker-controlled header byte bits_per_pixel (read at line 136 from the file, never validated or clamped) is assigned directly to image->depth, which scales 'length' past the pixel buffer capacity whenever depth exceeds the 32-bit quantum fixed by SetQuantumQuantum(quantum_info,32).

assumptions: GetQuantumExtent(image,quantum_info,quantum_type) returns the per-scanline byte capacity of the GetQuantumPixels(quantum_info) buffer, consistent with the universal ImageMagick coder pattern where extent is the value passed as the read count into the same buffer; SetQuantumQuantum(quantum_info,32) fixes samples at 32 bits so extent = columns*channels*4.
ReadBlobStream on a file-backed blob copies up to 'length' bytes into the supplied buffer (equivalent to ReadBlob), per standard ImageMagick blob semantics.
limitations: On 32-bit builds where ssize_t is 32-bit, the row loop bound '(ssize_t) image->rows' could wrap for rows near 2^32 and skip pixel reading (robustness, not corruption).

ImportQuantumPixels may consume bytes beyond 'count' from 'stream' when the computed 'length' is smaller than the 32-bit import width; those reads stay within the allocation and expose at most uninitialized data (robustness).
When image_info->ping is set, the function returns at line 348 before the sink; the trigger requires ping unset, which is the normal decode path.

verdict.summary: In the FTPWHO branch of dostor, when the attacker-controlled STOR filename length sl is exactly sizeof shm_data_cur->filename, the guard 'sl < sizeof shm_data_cur->filename' routes execution into the else arm, where the source index 'sl - sizeof shm_data_cur->filename - 1U' wraps to SIZE_MAX. The memcpy then reads one byte before the buffer holding name (out-of-bounds read) and copies it into the shared-memory filename field readable by local ftpwho users; for all sl >= N the copied window also omits any NUL terminator. No statement in the code bounds sl or corrects the index.

evidence.reason: Root cause: unsigned underflow in the source index. With sl == sizeof shm_data_cur->filename (instantiated trigger: FTP client sends STOR with a filename of exactly that length, reachable past the line-149 guard whose complement admits sl == N), 'sl - sizeof shm_data_cur->filename - 1U' evaluates to SIZE_MAX, so &name[SIZE_MAX] wraps to name - 1 and memcpy reads name[-1] out of bounds; the copied bytes also contain no NUL, leaving the shm filename unterminated.

Boundary guard whose complement under-admits the exact-limit value: it protects only the if arm (sl <= N-1, so filename[sl] at index <= N-1 is in bounds) and sends sl == N into the else arm whose index expression is valid only for sl >= N+1; this is the one guard whose wrong complement is the defect.

assumptions: The FTPWHO (and QUOTAS/WITH_TLS) sections are compiled in; shm_data_cur->filename is a fixed-size char array whose size N an attacker can match with a STOR argument of length N.

Internal callees (checknamesanity, get_atomic_file, ul_init, ul_send, ul_exit, tryautorename, quota_update, ul_quota_update) are not shown; their contracts cannot be quoted and were not used to dismiss or trigger any candidate.

The buffer holding 'name' is allocated by the command parser, which is not shown; the out-of-bounds byte at name[-1] is outside the string object 'name' designates regardless of adjacent allocation layout.
limitations: Possible uninitialized read (CWE-457): 'ULHandler ulhandler;' (line 3) has no initializer, and on the ul_init failure arm (lines 165-172, which writes only ret = -1) the reads 'uploaded += (unsigned long long) ulhandler.total_uploaded;' (line 192) and 'displayrate(MSG_UPLOADED, ulhandler.total_uploaded, ...)' (line 250) execute; the trigger requires ul_init to fail without initializing, which depends on an unshown callee and could not be instantiated per discipline 3.

TOCTOU: checknamesanity(name) at line 33 and the rename/open at lines 45/58 are ordered uses of an attacker-named path with no lock; O_NOFOLLOW at lines 58/60 guards the final symlink component at open, and the residual race requires attacker-controlled directory contents and a filesystem race win not exhibited in this code.
